screening.reason: Reports a 3-D CNN diagnostic classification of ASD vs NC using resting-state fMRI brain functional networks from the ABIDE-I NYU site (Inclusion 2, 3)

evidence_spans.text:
Results: We collected 79 ASD patients and 105 NCs from the ABIDE-I dataset.
The mean accuracy of our classiﬁcation algorithm was 77.74% for classiﬁcation
of ASD versus NCs.
evidence_spans.claim: A 3-D CNN classifying ASD vs NC from 79 ASD and 105 NC ABIDE-I subjects achieved 77.74% mean accuracy.

evidence_spans.text:
The ﬁrst phase of ABIDE (ABIDE-I)
compiles a dataset of 1112 individuals from 17 sites and
consists of 539 individuals with ASD and 573 typical controls. 
Since the scan parameters vary across sites, ABIDE is a highly
heterogeneous dataset. To avoid the impact of data heterogeneity,
we collected raw rs-fMRI data from the whole NYU site,
consisting of 79 ASD subjects and 105 normal controls (NCs).
evidence_spans.claim: To avoid cross-site heterogeneity, the study restricted analysis to the single NYU site of ABIDE-I (79 ASD, 105 NC) rather than the full 539/573 ABIDE-I sample.

evidence_spans.text:
We preprocessed the data using a widely adopted pipeline called
Conﬁgurable Pipeline for the Analysis of Connectomes (C-PAC)
(Craddock et al., 2013), which involves skull striping, slice timing
correction, realignment to correct for motion, and bandpass
ﬁltering (0.01–0.1 Hz).
evidence_spans.claim: Data were preprocessed with C-PAC (skull stripping, slice timing, motion realignment, bandpass filtering).

evidence_spans.text:
The independent
components were derived using Group-ICA, and further inspected to identify eight well deﬁned brain function networks (BFNs). (B) The selected BFNs were used to
extract subject-speciﬁc spatial maps using dual regression.
evidence_spans.claim: Eight brain functional networks were derived via group-ICA and subject-specific maps via dual regression, used as 3-D CNN input.

evidence_spans.text:
A total of 10-fold cross validation strategy was used for evaluating classiﬁcation
performance.
evidence_spans.claim: Classification performance was evaluated with 10-fold cross-validation.

evidence_spans.claim: A baseline model using all BFNs achieved 69.58% accuracy versus the proposed MCSE-VGG.
The proposed MCSE-VGG model using all BFNs achieved 77.74% accuracy, 76.74% precision, 78.57% recall, F1 75.33%.

evidence_spans.text:
The SN-dDMN and SN-LCEN pairs showed
increased connectivity strength in ASD, and hypo-connectivity
was observed in the PCUN-dDMN pair of ASD.
evidence_spans.claim: ASD showed hyperconnectivity between salience network (SN) and dorsal DMN, and between SN and left central executive network, and hypoconnectivity between precuneus and dorsal DMN.

evidence_spans.text:
Our ﬁndings support the under-connectivity hypnosis in
autism proposed by Just et al. (2004).
evidence_spans.claim: Findings are interpreted as supporting the under-connectivity hypothesis of autism.

assessments.support: N by diagnosis (79 ASD/105 NC), single site (NYU), and demographics (age, IQ, ADOS) are reported in Table 1; restriction to one site is explicitly justified as avoiding cross-site heterogeneity.
C-PAC pipeline, group-ICA-derived BFNs and dual regression are described in detail.

ADOS total/communication/social scores reported for the ASD group as part of Table 1, indicating ADOS-based diagnosis, though the exact diagnostic criterion/instrument sentence is not quoted verbatim.

Group-ICA and dual regression appear to have been performed on the full sample before the random train/validation split and 10-fold cross-validation, with no stated leakage control; no uncertainty interval is given around the single reported accuracy; site handling is not applicable (single site) but this also means findings are not tested for cross-site generalization.

risk_of_bias.summary: Cohort, pipeline and demographic/clinical reporting are thorough for this single-site (NYU) ABIDE-I subsample, but group-ICA/dual-regression feature derivation appears to precede the cross-validation split with no stated leakage control, and the single reported accuracy lacks an uncertainty interval; the deliberate single-site design avoids cross-site heterogeneity but means no site-generalization evidence is provided.

charting.title: Large-Scale Brain Functional Network Integration for Discrimination of Autism Using a 3-D Deep Learning Model
charting.disorder_diagnosis: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) vs Normal Control (NC)
charting.diagnosis_assessment: ADOS (total, communication and social scores reported for the ASD group)
charting.severity_levels: ADOS total 11.30 ± 4.08; ADOS communication 3.54 ± 1.55; ADOS social 7.76 ± 2.97
charting.age_matched: No — groups differed significantly in age (p=0.039), full IQ (p=0.022) and verbal IQ (p=0.001)
charting.dataset_openly_available: No — "further inquiries can be directed to the corresponding author/s" (no code or participant list released)
charting.dataset_available_request: Yes, upon inquiry to corresponding author
charting.specific_features: Eight group-ICA-derived brain functional networks (BFNs) with subject-specific spatial maps from dual regression
charting.feature_extraction_tools: C-PAC pipeline; Group-ICA + dual regression (no ROI atlas; data-driven ICA networks)
charting.importance_method: Per-BFN ablation (single-network models) and pairwise inter-BFN connectivity-strength comparison
charting.top_features_identified: Salience network (SN)-dorsal DMN, SN-left central executive network, and precuneus-dorsal DMN connections
charting.feature_change_direction: Hyperconnectivity in SN-dDMN and SN-LCEN pairs; hypoconnectivity in the PCUN-dDMN pair, in ASD vs NC
charting.model_category: 3-D convolutional neural network with channel-wise (squeeze-and-excitation) attention
charting.specific_algorithms: MCSE-VGG (modified 3-D VGG-Net with SE attention modules) vs a baseline 3-D CNN and single-BFN models
charting.key_performance_results: MCSE-VGG using all 8 BFNs: 77.74% accuracy, 76.74% precision, 78.57% recall, F1 75.33%, versus a baseline model using all BFNs at 69.58% accuracy
charting.summary_key_findings: A 3-D CNN with channel attention integrating eight group-ICA brain functional networks classified ASD vs NC in a single-site (NYU) ABIDE-I subsample (79 ASD/105 NC) with 77.74% accuracy, outperforming a baseline model (69.58%); ASD showed hyperconnectivity between the salience network and DMN/central executive network and hypoconnectivity between precuneus and dorsal DMN, consistent with the under-connectivity hypothesis of autism.
charting.features_associated_disorder: Increased SN-dDMN and SN-LCEN connectivity; decreased PCUN-dDMN connectivity

narrative_row.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction (ASD vs NC); ABIDE-I, single NYU site only, 79 ASD / 105 NC (full ABIDE-I: 539 ASD/573 TC across 17 sites)
narrative_row.methods: C-PAC-preprocessed rs-fMRI; group-ICA identified eight brain functional networks, subject-specific spatial maps via dual regression, classified with a modified 3-D VGG-Net with squeeze-and-excitation channel attention (MCSE-VGG); evaluated with 10-fold cross-validation.
narrative_row.outcomes: MCSE-VGG achieved 77.74% accuracy (76.74% precision, 78.57% recall, F1 75.33%) versus a 69.58%-accuracy baseline; ASD showed hyperconnectivity between the salience network and DMN/central executive network and hypoconnectivity between precuneus and dorsal DMN, consistent with the under-connectivity hypothesis.
narrative_row.key_limitations: Single-site design chosen to avoid cross-site heterogeneity, so no cross-site generalization evidence; no separate validation dataset; ASD and NC groups differed significantly in age and IQ; no motion/QC threshold or leakage-control statement; no code/participant list released.
narrative_row.relevance_notes: A well-documented single-site ABIDE-I predictive study illustrating a deliberate site-restriction strategy as an alternative to multi-site harmonisation.

kg_link.cohort_description: Single NYU site of ABIDE-I; 79 ASD, 105 NC, selected to avoid cross-site scan-parameter heterogeneity (full ABIDE-I: 539 ASD/573 TC, 17 sites)
kg_link.atlas: Data-driven group-ICA networks (8 brain functional networks), no fixed ROI atlas
kg_link.finding: A 3-D CNN with channel attention (MCSE-VGG) classified ASD vs NC with 77.74% accuracy (baseline 69.58%), and found hyperconnectivity between the salience network and DMN/central executive network and hypoconnectivity between precuneus and dorsal DMN in ASD.
